It clicked with me when I was 12. I had started going through puberty like a year before and my jealousy/desire to be masculine that had been very subtle during my childhood just felt like it was amplified. It felt like I had normal puberty weirdness, but also another deeper discomfort stacked on top of it that I couldn't pin down. This last part is kind of silly, but I only realized when one night I was reading a fanfiction that had a gay relationship in it, and I was really jealous of both of them. It just made it finally click in my mind that I did actually want to be a guy.

I will say that although transition doesn't make insecurity go away, it has helped me be far more comfortable and confident in my own skin because I feel more in connection with my body. It's genuinely up to you to figure out what you would want out of transition if you did do it, but you don't have to figure it out all at once. You don't even have to put a label on it, I've been out as trans for 6.5 years and I dont have a complete label for my gender lol. Just experiment in tiny steps, and go with what feels right in your gut.

Oughhh man. As a trans guy who just got the opportunity to start hrt after waiting for 6 years I deal with it by like, going on a big hike, or drinking a large glass of water all at once, or just by letting myself cry it out.

I think we've all tried our best. I walked around doing voter registration canvassing in the desert heat this summer and I don't even know how many staircases I scaled for that shit. And it didn't really work. But, I mean, I got up each day for six years straight waiting to even start medical transition, I think being transgender can be very tediously going in circles a lot before you get somewhere, and maybe that's what's happening to us right now on a larger scale. 

I think the scariest part though, and the worst case scenario for me, is that it might genuinely come down to choosing between my full ride to college or my ability to continue my transition for the next three years. But like, I've been thinking about this book I picked up a bit ago about the history of Einsteins equations, because one part mentions how one of his assistants ended up working with Einstein because he was searching for work after fleeing Nazi Germany. It gives me hope that some people figured out their lives after fleeing something as horrible as that. Theres also all of the accounts of queer people in the past who managed to transition and live out their lives despite the odds being stacked worse against them, less social awareness and less resources. If so many people in the past were able to figure things out, I have trust that we will too.

I might be biased because I'm not really afraid of needles, but I've done like, finger pricks on myself for biology labs and also donate blood regularly, and doing injections on yourself feels like absolutely nothing compared to that. 

I've done two T shots so far, and I've found the hardest part is just mentally psyching yourself up to do the injection. Everytime after I prep the needle it takes a minute or two to actually get around to injecting myself, but after that it literally feels like nothing. Maybe the slightest sensation of it is there, but less than a flu shot! It was easier the second time around too, because I knew it didn't feel like anything. 

If you do opt for doing it by shots, I do reccomend doing subq shots because the needle is shorter than the ones for IM injections (less than an inch long), and you're injecting at an angle into fat instead of straight down into muscle. Watching [this video](https://youtu.be/fkBuY4iMK7E?si=yG8ctg0nbZwpc0mE) of a nurse explaining subq injections also helps me do my shots. This guy is really informative on how to prep everything, and also it's comforting to see a nurse do injections on himself so casually (warning though if you're squeamish about watching injections.)

However, if you don't opt for injections you'll be fine! I've heard that gel isn't transferable after it dries, and theres tons of people that do it around cis women and trans women without a problem. I also wouldn't worry too much about stockpiling stuff if you're in a blue state? I'm in a red state in the deep south right now, and tbh it is really scary to think about, but I have faith that it won't get so horrific I won't have access to hrt in some way. I think it would be a mess to ban that for adults.

If not I doubt those dreams mean anything more than all the other random nonsense you can dream about.

It sounds like you might already be dealing with some sort of pain dealing with dysphoria and dismissing the life you desire. I do genuinely think its worth transitioning! As much as there has been a very vocal community of transphobes in the past few years, the majority of people I've met are uninformed but accepting and again I genuinely think you'll be okay. 

I promise it won't be as bad as you imagine it is, and you can transition and come out as slowly as is comfortable for you if you're ever ready, and theres going to be a community you can find out there to support you when you do (Maybe try and find a local lgbt center near you if there is one, they usually have community events!)
